annotation.kind: direct formalization of Theorems 3.3-3.4, equations (3.17) and (3.20), and Remark 4 with separately quantified algorithm families and qualitative first-order meaning

assumptions: Each separately quantified algorithm family has a positive dimension n, a nonsingular system A*xExact=b with b nonzero, increasing full-rank Algorithm 2 search spaces, and raw executions at every positive k<=n.
One fixed nonsingular nonidentity right preconditioner MR has certified actual inverses for MR and A*MR^-1, and the modular left preconditioner is the identity.

At the MGS-selected dimension, the computed basis applications satisfy (3.14), products with A satisfy (C.1), the inaccessible search basis satisfies (C.2), and rhoAR is the exact ratio (3.15) with positive denominator.

As stated in Appendix C and reused by Appendix D, an applicability hypothesis supplies the source MGS/Givens and solution-product error models and all five terms of (3.16) at every well-conditioned dimension satisfying the MGS terminal-or-near-dependence alternative, including the um*etaR*kappa(MR) term for flexible GMRES.

The uniform Appendix-C/D interfaces supply raw decompositions and sensitivity gains in actual perturbation magnitudes; they contain no selected dimension, c(n,k)-weighted component estimate, or final theorem bound.
Unqualified square kappa is interpreted uniformly as either the Frobenius or induced-2 condition number, both readings explicitly authorized by Section 2.

The unspecified c(n,k) is represented only by its nonnegative value at each fixed dimension, and qualitative smallness and omitted second-order terms are parameterized without a precision filter or invented threshold.
All modeled quantities are real, so exceptional floating-point values and range failures are outside the model.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p19_t3_right_flexible_attainable_forward_error {n : Nat} (semantics : P19FirstOrderSemantics) (choice : P19StaticSquareKappaChoice) : (forall right mgs appendixC applicability, exists k : P19Theorem31Dimension n, p19IterationWellConditioned (right.family.iteration k) and p19FirstOrderLe semantics (right relative forward error) (right.dimensionFactor * right three-source envelope)) and (forall flexible mgs appendixD applicability, exists k : P19Theorem31Dimension n, p19IterationWellConditioned (flexible.family.iteration k) and p19FirstOrderLe semantics (flexible relative forward error) (flexible.dimensionFactor * flexible two-source envelope)) and forall family preconditioner ug um ua etaR rhoAR, right envelope = flexible envelope + um*etaR*kappa(MR), where each applicability function supplies the complete source conditions at every well-conditioned terminal-or-near-dependence candidate
formal_statement.plain_language: For every right execution family and, separately, every fixed-preconditioner flexible execution family whose complete source conditions hold at each MGS-admissible candidate, the MGS analysis selects an iteration no larger than n and proves the corresponding three-term or two-term qualitative first-order forward-error bound there; the right envelope differs by exactly the fresh preconditioner-reapplication term.

informal_proof: For each variant independently, use a finite first-loss search on the MGS conditioning property: choose n if it remains well conditioned, otherwise choose the predecessor of the first failing dimension and invoke the cited near-dependence law. Obtain the complete source conditions at that candidate from the applicability hypothesis, apply the uniform Appendix-C or Appendix-D raw sensitivity expansion, derive the c(n,k)ug, c(n,k)um*etaR, and c(n,k)ua magnitude bounds from the actual perturbation models, combine the contributions with the Euclidean triangle inequality, and retain the source-classified second-order remainder. Expanding the two envelopes then isolates the right-only um*etaR*kappa(MR) term.
informal_statement: The complete conditional attainable-forward-error bounds (3.17) and (3.20), together with Remark 4's exact identification of the right-only preconditioner-reapplication term.
